findings.claim: The GWT-Koenig hypothesis proposes one full-focus plus stubbed channels as a token-bounded research-center reading policy and explicitly predicts failure on global comparison questions; it defines an effective-price break-even where two additional wrong fields erase the token savings.
findings.implication: Selection/compression quality must be evaluated separately for decision tasks and exhaustive-state-read tasks. Token reduction alone is not success; focus misses need explicit error cost.

findings.claim: The KoenigDB spec proposes an append-only, tiny derived fold with source pointer on every value; current state is latest value per key, historical state is ts<=T, and the database must be rebuildable from the authoritative source so it cannot become a second truth store.
findings.implication: This is a useful projection/cache pattern for current UnifiedDB: derived low-token views should be provenance-bound, rebuildable and subordinate to canonical semantic state. Do not import the literal koenig.db architecture as a new primary database.

findings.claim: The same spec treats a compact ziel= marker as a projection of a richer context/world facet: routing context is declared rather than guessed, while full provenance/time/status lives in the canonical layer. findings.implication: Preserve context/world as typed canonical semantics and allow cheap projections at transport boundaries; do not let projection fields become independent truth.
